title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving emergency Unconditional Cash (UCT) plus emergency agricultural inputs (cash+ approach) to HHs in Beletweyne to ensure vulnerable HHs’ immediate needs to food access are met.

description.narrative: ltpgtRDSA will target a population of 11040 individuals (Women 4100, girls 3,400, men 2,100 and boys 1992) in the Beletweyne district. The target populations live in rural Villages (Macruuf 186 HHs, Qoyda 123HHs, Shabelow 184HHs, Horjoog 58HHs, Dhaywabar 93HHs), and IDP sites (Nasri2 116HHs, Fatxi2 107HHs, Matanaha 193HHs, Mubarak 198HHs, Nasiib 149HHs, Tawakal Siigalow 193HHs, Nesteho 170HHs and Rasmi 70HHs. A population comprising 7,176 IDP individuals and the vulnerable host community of 3,864 individuals will benefit from this project. Based on the RDSA assessment report, 8,169 individuals in the above locations are from minority and marginalized groups with additional vulnerabilities assessed. In order to respond to this crisis, the Rural Development Support Agency (RDSA) will innovatively implement community-led and participatory lifesaving Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCT) plus agricultural inputs to (cash+ approach) to ensure vulnerable households’ immediate availability and access to food while also enabling them to produce locally and secure harvest/food stocks, sustain animal health and boost livestock production, and avert further livelihood assets depletion. These activities will be implemented in accordance with humanitarian and protection principles, with a significant focus on mainstreaming protection and inclusion for the most vulnerable displaced people due to the climate crisis in Beletweyne and surrounding villages. RDSA project in these locations will focus on under-served displacement sites and rural villages to improve access to unconditional multipurpose cash services to yield context-relevant and needs-driven emergency livelihood opportunities for affected communities. ltbrgtIn this project, RDSA aims to mitigate further depletion of existing livelihoods owned by vulnerable community members and mitigate displacement at the community level by injecting cash and agricultural support activities. As part of RDSA’s strategy and that the allocation of community ownership and sustainability will be enhanced through community participation and capacity-building Therefore, in all project locations, RDSA will form and train 10 community members (6 women and 5 men) as the village Response and conflict management committee – VRCMC, who will support the project implementation and monitoring. In addition, RDSA will disperse 304,500.00 USD unconditional cash to 1,450 (8,700) individuals of whom 70% are PWD, women-headed, child-headed, and minority communities. ltbrgtIn this project, RDSA, in consultation with community members, will map out vulnerable households with livelihood activities at the edge of depletion and advise them to take advantage of cash transfers. RDSA has carried out a survey for this project to help RDSA understand the capacities of the community to design context-appropriate livelihood opportunities and the Agricultural inputs approach. RDSA will mobilize communities to form self-help groups who, on their own initiative, will rehabilitate irrigation canals to extend water for farms in water-scarce locations. Additionally, in consultation with community members, RDSA will purchase basic farming tools to facilitate planting and harvesting for farmers from disabled, women and child-headed households, minorities, and marginalized families. RDSA will conduct market assessments to inform food and cash assistance transfer modalities within target locations 3 PDMs will be conducted after every transfer to ensure beneficiary satisfaction, feedback, and transfer impact is documented. RDSA will give priority to PDAD mitigation, forming a PDAD taskforce committee in the target location and will work closely with stakeholders, including local authorities, community members, leaders, and other SHF recipients during beneficiary selection and registration to ensure the right beneficiaries receive the assistance.ltbrgtlt/pgt
